gloss: refined white sugar; superior white sugar

definitions.gloss: refined white sugar; superior white sugar
definitions.explanation: The most common type of granulated white sugar used in Japan, finer and slightly more moist than Western granulated sugar.

examples.japanese: {上白糖|じょうはくとう}を{大|おお}さじ{二杯|にはい}{加|くわ}える。
examples.english: Add two tablespoons of refined white sugar.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{家庭|かてい}では{上白糖|じょうはくとう}が{最|もっと}もよく{使|つか}われる{砂糖|さとう}だ。
examples.english: In Japanese households, refined white sugar is the most commonly used sugar.

examples.japanese: {上白糖|じょうはくとう}はグラニュー{糖|とう}と{比|くら}べて{粒|つぶ}が{細|こま}かく、{料理|りょうり}に{溶|と}けやすいのが{特徴|とくちょう}だ。
examples.english: Compared to granulated sugar, refined white sugar has finer grains and dissolves more easily in cooking.

notes:
Literally "superior white sugar," from {上|じょう} (superior), {白|はく} (white), and {糖|とう} (sugar). This is the default sugar in Japan — when Japanese recipes simply call for {砂糖|さとう} (sugar), they typically mean {上白糖|じょうはくとう}.

Unlike the coarser granulated sugar (グラニュー{糖|とう}) common in Western countries, {上白糖|じょうはくとう} has a finer texture and contains a small amount of inverted sugar, giving it a slightly moist quality and milder sweetness. It accounts for roughly half of all sugar consumption in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {上白糖|じょうはくとう}{大|おお}さじ{一杯|いっぱい}: one tablespoon of white sugar
- {上白糖|じょうはくとう}を{加|くわ}える: to add white sugar
- {上白糖|じょうはくとう}の{代|か}わりに: instead of white sugar

SIMILAR WORDS:
- グラニュー{糖|とう}: granulated sugar — coarser crystals, commonly used in Western baking
- {三温糖|さんおんとう}: light brown sugar — made by further heating white sugar, with a richer flavor
- {黒糖|こくとう}: brown sugar, raw sugar — unrefined sugar from Okinawa with a strong molasses flavor
